subject: EU in-region routing & deletion controls — technical Q&A
messages:

Cc: Legal Ops <legal@medfirst.de>

Subject: EU-only processing / backups deletion questions (preliminary questionnaire attached)

Hi Vivek and Lauren,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Medifirst's legal and engineering teams have a few follow-ups before we move to a formal pilot. Attached is our initial SCCs and data residency questionnaire. The key asks from our side:

- Can Redwood guarantee that customer content for Medifirst can be routed and processed only in EU regions (data plane) for both hosted and dedicated modes?
- What does deletion look like for primary data and for backups/replicas? Our standard requirement is verifiable deletion within 30 days and removal of any backups within 90 days unless explicitly retained.
- We need a mapping between Redwood contractual safeguards (SCCs) and the technical controls (routing, KMS, operator access, audit logs).

Could you confirm whether you can provide a short technical mapping and an attestation template that our legal team can use? Also please include any limitations around automatic fallbacks (e.g., if EU capacity is exhausted).

Appreciate a brief response with expected timelines — Legal is hoping to review a formal attestation by next week.

Best,
Alice
Alice Müller
Head of IT Procurement, MediFirst GmbH

Subject: Re: EU-only processing / backups deletion questions (preliminary questionnaire attached)

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: yes, we support an EU-only data plane for both Hosted (with region pinning) and Dedicated modes; we offer Private deployment for fully customer-managed control planes. I'll attach a short control-plane summary and our initial SCCs->technical-controls mapping.

Key points:
- Routing: We support per-customer region pinning. Requests from Medifirst can be routed to EU-only inference clusters; capacity-based fallbacks are configurable per-customer (default: no cross-border fallback; optional: allow fallback to a pre-agreed region with explicit notification).
- Deletion: Primary content deletion is initiated immediately on request. For Hosted customers, deletion of all live replicas completes within 48 hours; backups (cold snapshots) are purged on a 30/60/90 configurable cadence — default retrospective deletion window is 90 days unless you request acceleration. We can commit to an attested 30-day operational deletion SLA for primary data; backup timelines require contract amendment for 30-day guaranteed backup removal.
- Encryption & keys: Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) available for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers can use our managed keys or a partner-managed KMS with DH key wrapping.
- Operator access & audit logs: All operator actions are logged and available through an audit export. For Private deployments logs are locally retained; for Hosted we provide a signed export on request and longer retention as a paid add-on.

I'm attaching a short PDF (redwood-eu-controlplane-summary.pdf) and we'll follow up with a CSV mapping to SCC clauses.

Action items for internal follow-up: @lauren please confirm the default backup purge cadence and whether Legal can get a template attestation. @karthik can you drop the SCCs mapping and note any limitations on fallbacks or third-party telemetry?

Thanks — Vivek

Attachment: redwood-eu-controlplane-summary.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing / backups deletion questions (preliminary questionnaire attached)

Vivek — adding detail for Legal & Engineering:

- Default backup retention (Hosted): snapshots are retained 90 days. We can offer a contract option for 30-day backup purging for EU-only customers, but that requires Reserved retention guarantees and additional operational controls (no cross-region replication for those snapshots).
- Deletion workflow: when a deletion request is received (API or support ticket) we: 1) mark data as deleted; 2) remove live replicas; 3) add deletion event to audit log with signer; 4) schedule snapshot purge job. For Dedicated & Private, we provide deletion runbook and a deletion certificate with hashes.
- SCCs mapping: most SCCs clauses map to our controls as follows:
  - SCCs Art. X (transfer restrictions) -> Region pinning + contractual restriction (no fallback)
  - SCCs Art. Y (access controls) -> KMS + role-based operator access + privileged access reviews
  - SCCs Art. Z (logs and evidence) -> Audit export + retention options

Limitations & notes: automated model hot-fallback is primarily a capacity optimization and is disabled by default for EU-only customers. If Medifirst requests cross-border fallback we need explicit signed consent and will outline risk acceptance language in the amendment.

I'll prepare a short attestation template for Legal to use and circulate tomorrow.

-Lauren
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Müller <alice.mueller@medfirst.de>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: EU-only processing / backups deletion questions (preliminary questionnaire attached)

Hi all — technical mapping attached (sccs-mapping-table.csv) and a few clarifications on routing and backups: 

- Routing policy implementation: we use request-level metadata + customer region tag to decide placement. For Hosted we run inference clusters in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt); customers choose a primary region and we only route to that region unless the "fallback_policy" flag is enabled. The fallback pipeline performs capability checks and only triggers when the primary region is unavailable for X minutes and queued requests exceed threshold T.
- Backups: cold snapshots are stored encrypted at rest in the chosen region. Replication to a secondary EU region is possible but not enabled by default for EU-only customers. Purge job removes snapshot objects and clears references in metadata store; we can produce a signed deletion manifest for each purge run.
- Operator access: we maintain a separation of duties: SREs have machine-level access in our internal VLAN but keys to decrypt customer data are never available to the operator unless customer grants a KMS grant. All operator sessions are recorded and searchable.

Links: control plane diagram (internal) available here: https://drive.redwood.internal/eu-controlplane-arch-2026

Attachment: sccs-mapping-table.csv

If Medifirst wants to proceed, Vivek / Lauren can share timeline for an attestation and an amendment for 30-day backup purge guarantee.

Thanks,
Karthik
